3. VERIFY THE SUPPLIED FRACTIONAL LOEWNER INTEGRAL

Put R=exp(x)>0,S=exp(y)>0. The proposed integral is exactly

 K_r(x,y)=(sin(pi r)/pi)(RS)^(r-.5)(R^2-1)(S^2-1)
    integral_0^infinity t^(1-r)/[(1+t)(R^2+t)(S^2+t)]dt. (I)

To check it, write k=1-r in (0,1). The standard scalar integral, proved
by partial fractions of the positive-power Stieltjes integral, is
F_k(v)=(v^k-1)/(v-1)
       =(sin(pi k)/pi) integral_0^infinity t^k/[(1+t)(v+t)]dt.
Its negative divided difference is
 [F_k(b)-F_k(a)]/(a-b)
       =(sin(pi k)/pi) integral_0^infinity t^k/[(1+t)(a+t)(b+t)]dt.
Multiply by (a-1)(b-1), a=R^2,b=S^2. The numerator is
a b^k-b a^k+a^k-b^k-a+b, divided by a-b. Directly expanding (K)
gives exactly (RS)^(r-.5) times this expression. Since sin(pi k)=sin(pi r),
this proves (I). Coincident-node and node1 values follow by continuity.

4. REDUCE THE IMPROVED COEFFICIENT TO AN EXACT HARDY FRACTION

Let d_r(R)=R^(r-.5)(R+1), b_r(R)=R/d_r(R)=R^(1.5-r)/(R+1),
and eta_r=sin(pi r)/(1+|cos(pi r)|).
Factor the possibly signed diagonal R-1 and then the positive diagonal
d_r(R) from K_r-eta_r L_0, with L_0=(R-1)(S-1)/(R+S).
Substitute t=u^2 in (I) and use the exact Carleman identity
integral_0^infinity du/[(R^2+u^2)(S^2+u^2)]=pi/[2RS(R+S)].
The remaining sufficient quadratic inequality is

 ||B_r(iu) U(u)||_2^2 >= [eta_r/sin(pi r)] ||V(u)||_2^2,
 U(u)=sum_i v_i/(R_i^2+u^2),
 V(u)=sum_i v_i b_r(R_i)/(R_i^2+u^2),
 B_r(z)=z^(1.5-r)/(1+z), Re z>0,                       (P)

where norms integrate the full real boundary and v_i are arbitrary complex.
All products are L^2. The pole-cancellation proof from the frozen entropy
Hardy argument applies unchanged: the analytic remainder is bounded near0
and O(1/z) uniformly on the right half-plane. Consequently

 P_-[B_r(iu)U(u)]=P_-V(u)
